of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are mandatory and the same are applicable to all the Sameerudheen E vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8128161/

4.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010(4) KLT 706(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sameerudheen E vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The question involved in this case is the non- compliance of the mandatory provisions contained under Section 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
As there was a divergent view in the matter, the decision in Gopalakrishnan (supra) along with the other decisions of the learned Single Judges were referred to the Division Bench.

The Division Bench of this Court in Crl.R.P.No.1814/2002 considered the said question and has disposed of the matter through order dated 17.11.2015 thereby upholding the view taken by this Court in Gopalakrishnan (supra).
5. Matters being so, the continued prosecution of the petitioner in C.C.No.1029/2014 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Parappanangadi, Malappuram District, are illegal and no purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter any further.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Parappanangadi, Malappuram District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The matters involved in the said case are quite unnecessary in view of the decisions noted supra and therefore, the same are liable to be quashed.

In the result, this Crl.M.C. is allowed and Annexure-A complaint on the basis of analysis report and all further proceedings initiated against the petitioner in C.C.No.1029/2014 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Parappanangadi, Malappuram District, are hereby quashed.
